Theorem
[Tachibana rigidity]

Source: petersen:page-0367 ↗ thm:pet-ch9-curvature-tensor-lichnerowicz ↗ prop:pet-ch9-vanishing-connection-laplacian ↗ conv:pet-ch9-so-metric-convention 1. ch9:9.4.8On a closed manifold, divergence-free curvature together with $\mathfrak R\ge 0$ implies $ abla R=0$. If the curvature operator is positive, the metric has constant sectional curvature.
Proof

↗ thm:pet-ch9-tachibana-parallel-curvature \sketch The curvature identity subsection 4.2, the lower bound in subsection 3.3, and subsection 3.1 imply $ abla R=0$. Under $\mathfrak R>0$, the argument from subsection 4.4 gives $LR=0$ for every $L\in \mathfrak {so}(T_pM)$. Choosing rotations that exchange an arbitrary vector with an orthogonal one and polarizing shows all mixed curvature components vanish. Every decomposable bivector is consequently an eigenvector of $\mathfrak R$, forcing $\mathfrak R=kI$.

□
